- `Features/Game/GameBoardView.swift` — the actual board: stock (tap-to-draw/recycle), waste (fanned last-3 for draw-3 visibility, only the true top card selectable), 4 foundations keyed by `Suit`, 7 tableau columns fanned with real overlap math. Fixed a real identity bug before it could bite: was using positional `id: \.offset` in the tableau/waste `ForEach`s, switched to `id: \.element.id` — positional IDs would make SwiftUI think a "slot" changed rather than "a card left" once real transit animations get wired, which is exactly wrong for what `DealOrchestrator` is for.

## Integration recap — round 5

The reported failure this round was the *identical* error as last round — pbxproj still referencing the deleted `Domain/StuckDetection.swift`. Two consecutive rounds with the same stale-file error means my "the harness regenerates the project every time" theory from round 3 was wrong; the more consistent explanation is it only generates a project when none exists. So I deleted the stale `.xcodeproj` again — `project.yml` (unchanged, correct) is the real source of truth, and this forces a clean regeneration next build instead of failing on a two-round-old dangling reference forever.

Reading through this round's actual new work, I found and fixed three more real bugs before they could compound:

**Copy divergence, exactly as both lanes flagged.** `Interaction/RecoveryCopy.swift` and `Persistence/AppRestoreCoordinator.swift` were built in parallel, both hardcoding near-identical recovery strings — and the settings one had already drifted ("Couldn't restore settings" vs. "Couldn't save settings"). Had `AppRestoreCoordinator`'s two message properties delegate to `RecoveryCopy` instead, so there's exactly one wording source again.

**A real compile bug nobody's cross-review caught:** `AppRestoreCoordinator.restoreAll(gameStore:statsStore:settingsStore:)` took the concrete `GameSaveStore`/`StatsLogStore`/`SettingsStore` types as parameters — but its own test file passes a generic `TrackedStore<Model>` mock to it, which is an unrelated type that would never type-check against a concrete parameter. Made `restoreAll` generic over anything conforming to `PersistenceStore` with the matching `Model`, which is clearly what the test (and the mock's whole design) already assumed.

**A one-letter-typo compile bug in this round's new adversarial stuck-detector test:** `DrawThreeStuckDetectorTests.canMoveAsWasteTop` called `MoveValidation.isLegal(...)` — but `isLegal` only exists on `MoveValidator` (the actual rules type), not `MoveValidation` (the older delegating-wrapper enum with near-identical name). Fixed both call sites.

**One more thing worth naming precisely, not just "GameEngine is missing":** `SolitaireTabHost.swift` directly instantiates `StatsView()` and `SettingsView()` — neither exists anywhere in the tree. Claude A was explicit that she stopped short of building those screens this round (real architectural gap: `SettingsStore`/`StatsLogStore` aren't observable, so there's no way to bind them to SwiftUI yet), but `SolitaireTabHost` still references them as if they exist. So the actual compile blocker list for this round's UI work is three named types — `GameEngine`, `StatsView`, `SettingsView` — not one.

Everything else checked out: `DrawThreeStuckDetector`'s hardening and its buried-legal-move adversarial fixture are logically sound (I traced the fixture by hand — the ace of hearts really is buried at position 4 of the stock cycle and really is the only legal move), `GameBoardView`'s pile-position accessibility composition is correct, and the `AccessibilityID` usage throughout is accurate to the real file (not guessed).

Where things stand: this is now five rounds in, and the single blocking gap is unchanged — no `GameEngine`. Everything else (domain rules, persistence with a now-fixed corruption-vs-fresh-install distinction, the full card visual system, the deal/flip planner, terminal overlays, a real board layout, restore coordination) is built and, as far as careful reading can confirm, correct. But none of it can compile together until `GameEngine` exists, and now `StatsView`/`SettingsView` are also explicitly missing rather than just deferred.

- **data_domain (Codex A):** `GameEngine` is now the single most urgent piece of work in this entire build — it's blocking every other lane. It needs to own board state, call `MoveValidator`/`RunRelocation` for execution, `UndoStack`, timer, `StuckDetector` selection by draw mode, and expose whatever `GameView`/`GameBoardView` already assume (`state`, `interaction`, `selectCard(pile:index:)`, `attemptMove(to:)`, `drawFromStock()`, `undo()`, `newGame(drawMode:requiresConfirmation:)`).
- **primary_ui (Claude A/B):** once `GameEngine` lands, build the real `StatsView`/`SettingsView` — but first someone needs to actually decide the observable-bridge question Claude A raised (does `GameEngine` grow a settings/stats echo, or does a lightweight observable wrapper get injected at the app root?).
